# LibcameraSharp

> A .NET 10 SDK for cameras driven by libcamera, mostly Raspberry Pi camera modules: photos (JPEG, PNG, DNG with EXIF), H.264 and MJPEG video (MP4, Matroska, MPEG-TS), live frames, and typed camera controls. NuGet package `LibcameraSharp`; `LibcameraSharp.Core` is libcamera itself for .NET. Linux arm64, libcamera 0.7.

Everything is in the `LibcameraSharp` namespace. The pattern: open a `CameraDevice`, declare an options record (`PhotoOptions`, `VideoOptions`, `FrameOptions`), and pass it to the call. There is no separate configure step; passing the same options again doesn't set the camera up again. Each options record has `Streams` (sizes, formats, raw; changing them reconfigures the camera) and `Controls` (exposure, gain, focus; the call waits until they take effect).

```csharp
using LibcameraSharp;

using CameraDevice camera = CameraDevice.Open();

Photo photo = await camera.CapturePhotoAsync(new PhotoOptions
{
    Controls = new CameraControls { Exposure = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(8), Gain = 2.0f },
});
await photo.SaveAsync("photo.jpg");

await using (VideoRecording recording = camera.RecordTo("clip.mp4"))
    await Task.Delay(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));

await foreach (VideoFrame frame in camera.ReadFramesAsync(new FrameOptions(), ct))
    using (frame)                                        // frames are the camera's buffers: always dispose
        Process(frame.Plane(0), frame.Stride(0));
```

Things an assistant gets wrong without being told:

- `camera.RecordTo(...)` returns a `VideoRecording`; disposing it finalises the file.
- `Exposure = TimeSpan.Zero` and `Gain = 0` mean "back to automatic"; `null` means "don't send".
- Rows can be padded: use `frame.Stride(i)`, not the width.
- `BGR888` is stored R, G, B in memory (libcamera names read backwards).
- One process holds a camera at a time; a second gets `CameraBusyException`.
- On a camera with autofocus a photo focuses first; set `Controls.Focus` to skip that.
- Without a camera (tests, a laptop): derive from `CameraDevice` (protected constructor, virtual members) and build return values with `LibcameraSharpModelFactory`.

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://github.com/linckez/LibcameraSharp/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md): install, first photo, options
- [Photos](https://github.com/linckez/LibcameraSharp/blob/main/docs/photos.md): formats, EXIF, raw and DNG
- [Video](https://github.com/linckez/LibcameraSharp/blob/main/docs/video.md): recording, containers, streaming to a browser from ASP.NET Core
- [Frames](https://github.com/linckez/LibcameraSharp/blob/main/docs/frames.md): pixels into your own code, formats, strides
- [Controls](https://github.com/linckez/LibcameraSharp/blob/main/docs/controls.md): exposure, gain, focus, zoom, and when they take effect
- [Cameras](https://github.com/linckez/LibcameraSharp/blob/main/docs/cameras.md): choosing a camera, sensor modes
- [Raspberry Pi setup](https://github.com/linckez/LibcameraSharp/blob/main/docs/raspberry-pi.md): checking the camera, deploying, troubleshooting
- [LibcameraSharp.Core](https://github.com/linckez/LibcameraSharp/blob/main/docs/core.md): libcamera itself: configurations, buffers, requests

## Examples

- [PhotoBooth](https://github.com/linckez/LibcameraSharp/tree/main/demo/PhotoBooth): a console app
- [StreamingCamera](https://github.com/linckez/LibcameraSharp/tree/main/demo/StreamingCamera): an ASP.NET Core webcam
